territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons who promote, advertise or conduct business in Texas, produce products or services used by Texas residents, or develop or deploy AI systems in Texas.

evidence.quote: produces a product or service used by residents of this state

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Texas H.B. 149 creates Business & Commerce Code Subtitle D on artificial intelligence: prohibited AI uses, a consumer disclosure duty, Attorney General enforcement with civil penalties, a regulatory sandbox and an AI council, and amends biometric and processor rules. Effective January 1, 2026.
summary.long: The Act adds Business & Commerce Code Subtitle D. Chapter 551 defines AI system and applicability to persons who do business in Texas, produce products used by Texas residents, or develop or deploy AI in Texas. Chapter 552 requires governmental agencies and health care providers to disclose AI interaction to consumers and bars AI developed or deployed to incite self-harm or crime, government social scoring, government biometric identification without consent, intentional unlawful discrimination, and listed deepfake and child-sexual material. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement, with a 60-day cure notice, civil penalties of $10,000 to $12,000 for curable violations, $80,000 to $200,000 for uncurable ones, and $2,000 to $40,000 per day for continued violations, and no private right of action. Chapter 553 creates a sandbox for up to 36 months of testing with waivers of certain laws, except Subchapter B of Chapter 552. Chapter 554 creates a seven-member Texas Artificial Intelligence Council with advisory powers and no power to adopt binding rules. The Act amends Business & Commerce Code Sections 503.001 (biometric identifiers, including AI training exemptions) and 541.104 (processor duties), and state agency review and IT reporting rules. Section 9 conditions certain agency duties on appropriations. Effective January 1, 2026.

notes: Section 2 quotes subsection (a) and (e) changes; the existing subsection (b) is not reproduced, so (b-1)'s reference to Subsection (b) cannot be checked against the text. Bracketed deletions and underlining in amended sections are shown as plain text. Section 552.054 defines biometric data separately from §503.001's biometric identifier. Section 9 makes mandatory duties of agencies conditional on appropriations. Section 552.101(b) excludes a private right of action. Section 8 sets a September 1, 2026 posting deadline; Section 10 sets effect from January 1, 2026. "Artificial intelligence system" means any machine-based system that, for any explicit or implicit objective, infers from the inputs the system receives how to generate outputs
"Deployer" means a person who deploys an artificial intelligence system for use in this state.
"Developer" means a person who develops an artificial intelligence system that is offered, sold, leased, given, or otherwise provided in this state.
"Consumer" means an individual who is a resident of this state acting only in an individual or household context.
"Governmental entity" means any department, commission, board, office, authority, or other administrative unit of this state or of any political subdivision of this state
